note: The flow-skeleton PATTERN directory -- a layer distinct from the sink/source CATALOGUE (models/) and from the kind->evaluator recipe (evaluators.json). The catalogue labels what a single node IS (this call is an alloc, this arg is a size). A PATTERN here is a structural query over the SHAPE of the taint-scoped control skeleton produced for one function -- an ordered, nesting-aware sequence of {control | sink} events. A double-free is not one node the catalogue can name; it is two `free` nodes on one path with no reallocation between them. That shape only exists at this layer. Pure data: each pattern names the skeleton alphabet it needs and the shape it matches; the engine that runs it lives outside this repo. Matches are LEADS, never verdicts.

skeleton_alphabet.note: What a rendered control skeleton puts on a line, and the per-sink facts a pattern predicates over. `emitted` marks whether the reader currently stamps that sink family onto the skeleton; a pattern requiring an un-emitted family is tier 2 (blocked) until the reader emits it.

per_sink_facts.tainted: the taint run reaches this sink's obligation value (bool) -- EMITTED
per_sink_facts.cap: destination_capacity status: within-capacity | exceeds-capacity | capacity-known-size-unknown | unknown -- EMITTED as the sink's `bound` axis (bounded|unbounded)
per_sink_facts.dom: guard dominance: guarded-region (checked) | fall-through (guard exists, sink escapes it) | none-observed (no size guard) -- EMITTED as the sink's `guarded` flag
per_sink_facts.size_expression: the size/length operand as written -- EMITTED as `size_expr` on the sink token (the operand at the catalog's size_arg)
per_sink_facts.control_nesting: the ordered enclosing control headers (outermost->innermost) the sink sits under -- EMITTED as `control` on the sink token, e.g. ["for"], ["if","while"]; keywords normalized (else->if)
per_sink_facts.dst: the destination pointer identity -- EMITTED as `dst` on the sink token (an allocator's assigned var, or a copy's arg0), so alloc-dst can be joined to copy-dst on one path
per_sink_facts.line: source line -- gives flow order and nesting within the function -- EMITTED

control_alphabet.note: The reader attaches enclosing control headers to each sink token as an ordered `control` list (outermost->innermost), NOT as standalone skeleton events. So loop/branch nesting of a sink is queryable today; the jump keywords and case labels are not yet materialized as their own events.

patterns.name: Buffer write reached around its size guard
patterns.shape: a memory.copy sink whose obligation value has dom == 'fall-through' -- a size-testing branch exists in the function but this copy is reached on the path that skips it
patterns.signal: the escaped guard is the lead; taint is a stronger corroboration, not required
patterns.note: implemented as the `missing-guard` evaluator + guard dimension (evaluators.json). Listed so the directory is complete.

patterns.name: Allocation size is attacker-influenced and unbounded
patterns.shape: a memory.alloc sink with tainted == true and cap in {exceeds-capacity, capacity-known-size-unknown}
patterns.signal: the size flows from a source and is not clamped to a bound
patterns.note: covered by the `relational` evaluator over alloc-size kinds.

patterns.name: Copy is enabled by an inverted capacity guard
patterns.shape: a tainted copy whose normalized size expression is on the left of a strict-or-equal greater-than capacity comparison in a dominating guard
patterns.signal: the guarded arm permits the copy when delivered length is at or beyond capacity
patterns.note: uses the generic comparator-aware evaluator over translator-provided guard predicates; no language-specific variable names are assumed.

patterns.name: Arithmetic addition precedes a memory bound check
patterns.shape: a tainted memory-size sink dominated by a guard whose normalized predicate adds values before comparing against an upper bound
patterns.signal: the addition can wrap before the bound comparison and invalidate the memory-safety check
patterns.note: generic expression-shape coverage for arithmetic-overflow-driven memory safety; language-specific range proofs remain future refinement.

patterns.name: Pointer arithmetic is performed before validation
patterns.shape: a pointer derived through arithmetic is later dereferenced on the same path before the source offset is validated
patterns.signal: the computed pointer may already be invalid when the later validation executes
patterns.note: the semantic graph preserves the derived pointer and later dereference order; the matcher does not reparse source expressions.

patterns.name: Copy inside a loop with no bound on the iteration length
patterns.substrate: the semantic sink event carries `control` (its enclosing for/while/do nesting) and `guarded`; the matcher consumes both facts.
patterns.shape: a memory.copy sink whose `control` list contains a for/while/do header, with guarded == false and the loop bound not derived from the destination capacity
patterns.signal: the loop can iterate past the destination; the copy is not guarded per-iteration
patterns.note: shipped in the semantic skeleton matcher: the copy sink's `control` nesting + `guarded` flag carry the loop-membership, so no separate control event is needed.

patterns.name: Allocate with one size, copy with another on the same path
patterns.substrate: each semantic sink event carries `dst` (the pointer identity) and `size_expr` (the size operand); path-local matcher state compares an allocation sink with a later copy sink sharing that destination.
patterns.shape: a memory.alloc token with dst==D, size_expr==sizeA followed on the same path by a memory.copy token with dst==D, size_expr==sizeB where sizeB is not syntactically derived from sizeA
patterns.signal: the destination was sized for sizeA but written sizeB
patterns.note: two-token path pattern joining alloc.dst to copy.dst; both dst and size_expr now emitted on every alloc/copy token.

patterns.name: Tainted unbounded write reaches a memory sink
patterns.shape: a buffer-write or buffer-size sink whose tainted obligation is unbounded relative to the destination
patterns.signal: the delivered write length is attacker-influenced and not discharged by a bound
patterns.note: The evaluator name remains `relational`; this public ID distinguishes write-size findings from tainted allocation-size findings.

patterns.name: Allocated object remains live at an exit
patterns.shape: an allocation origin reaches an enclosing exit without release, escape, or a surviving ownership alias
patterns.signal: the object is no longer recoverable by the owning scope
patterns.note: Path-specific leak matching remains in the semantic graph; Atropos supplies the public taxonomy.

patterns.name: Freed pointer is passed or compared as a value
patterns.shape: a freed object is passed, compared, or returned without a storage dereference
patterns.signal: the value use preserves a dangling pointer beyond its lifetime
patterns.note: This is intentionally distinct from use-after-free dereference findings.

patterns.name: Free reached twice on one path (double free)
patterns.shape: two memory.free sinks on the same path over the same pointer identity with no reassignment or reallocation of that pointer between them
patterns.signal: the second free is the lead
patterns.note: canonical typestate example. Matched PATH-SENSITIVELY: the reader replays a START->ALLOCATED->FREED property automaton as a forward may-analysis over the control-flow graph, so two frees on mutually-exclusive branches never meet (no false lead) while a free reachable across a loop back-edge does. Pointer identity is the alloc's destination variable.

patterns.name: Dereference or copy of a pointer after it was freed
patterns.shape: a memory.free(x) followed on the same path by a memory.deref(x) or a memory.copy reading from x, with no reassignment of x between
patterns.signal: the post-free use is the lead
patterns.note: The semantic graph emits READ_STORAGE, WRITE_STORAGE, PASS_VALUE, COMPARE_VALUE, and RETURN_VALUE, so both direct dereferences and value uses are matched path-sensitively.

patterns.name: Failed reallocation loses the only owning slot
patterns.shape: REALLOC_FAILED followed by WRITE_STORAGE(slot, NULL) and LOST_FROM_SLOT(object, slot), with no release or surviving alias before exit
patterns.signal: the failed realloc path drops the last owning slot; an existing alias suppresses this leak
patterns.note: The semantic graph matcher treats realloc failure as non-freeing, then evaluates slot loss and alias roots at the enclosing exit.

patterns.name: Dereference of a known-null storage slot
patterns.shape: WRITE_STORAGE(slot, NULL) followed on a compatible path by READ_STORAGE or WRITE_STORAGE through that slot
patterns.signal: the storage slot is proven null at the dereference
patterns.note: NULL is represented as a WRITE_STORAGE fact with null=true, keeping the event alphabet uniform.

patterns.name: Address of a local returned or stored past its scope
patterns.shape: a return (or store into an out-param / global) of the address of a stack local
patterns.signal: the escaping address is the lead
patterns.note: the semantic reader marks returned automatic arrays and explicit address-of-local paths; the matcher emits a use-after-return witness.

patterns.name: Return value dereferenced without a null/error check
patterns.shape: a call whose return is bound to r, then a memory.deref(r) on a path with no if/guard testing r between the call and the deref
patterns.signal: the unchecked deref is the lead
patterns.note: the semantic reader marks pointer call results as nullable origins; compatible NONNULL/ISNULL guards discharge the unchecked-return obligation before dereference.

build_order: Tier 1 runs over the semantic sink alphabet: missing-bounds, tainted-unbounded allocation, loop-contained copies, and allocation/copy size mismatch are shipped through the Atropos evaluator and semantic matcher.

Tier 2 lifetime facts are emitted by the semantic reader: free/release and dereference identities share the same field-sensitive object graph, with address-of-local escape and nullable return-origin facts.
The semantic matcher runs double-free, UAF, use-after-return, unchecked-return-deref, realloc-failure-leak, and null-deref patterns path-sensitively.
